Renaming the parameter or threading a tenantId argument through is out of Plan 100B-03's declared file scope (does not touch leave-check.ts); the general gap this exception documents is exactly what Issue #101 (T6, CONTEXT.md canonical_refs) exists to close — 'was hier nicht sauber getrennt wird, braucht dort eine Ausnahme'.

The documented anti-pattern this whole plan exists to forbid going forward (100B-CONTEXT.md D-07 <interfaces>: 'confirmed-saldo.ts:43 — THE ANTI-PATTERN'). Takes 'app: FastifyInstance' and reaches app.prisma directly (F1 wrong type/name, F2 FastifyInstance present) and its 'employeeId' parameter has no 'tenantId' sibling (F3) — its own docstring says 'PURE READ, no tenant argument. Callers MUST already have a tenant-scoped employeeId', which is exactly the convention F3 exists to stop being silently invisible once behind a facade. Plan 100B-07 converts this function to the db: Prisma.TransactionClient shape and removes this entry.

Plan 100B-04: a pure, side-effect-free type-mapping helper (EmployeeScope -> a Prisma 'where' fragment) with no Prisma CALL and no database client of any kind in its signature — D-07's whole point (a write silently leaving the caller's $transaction through app.prisma) cannot occur here because there is no client to call through. F1 is checked mechanically against every exported function declaration under contexts/*/facade/ regardless of whether it touches Prisma at all, so this genuinely-safe function is still visited and flagged. Scoping F1 itself to 'only functions with a db-shaped first parameter' would change lint-facade-signatures.ts, which is outside this plan's declared files_modified; a named exception is the cheaper, equally-auditable fix the plan's own Task 3 offers as the alternative.

Plan 100B-06 (D-08/T-100B-25): this is a HARD delete (OvertimeAccount.deleteMany, cascading to OvertimeTransaction) invoked ONLY from platform/api/employees.ts's DELETE /:id/hard-delete sequence, whose handler validates 'id' against req.user.tenantId at its own top (employee.findUnique({ where: { id, tenantId: req.user.tenantId } }), employees.ts:1108-1111) BEFORE the hard-delete $transaction — and therefore before this function — is ever reached. Adding a tenantId parameter here would be a decorative constraint with no independent identifier to check it against (there is no second, untrusted employeeId in play), not a real tenant boundary; the real boundary is the caller's own upstream validation, named explicitly here per D-08's 'named, not uniform' rule.
